Well that's pretty simple to translate if you want to weighting the results in the way you're talking about. The full release of the polliing data likely has all the info you need to do this.

  • If the sample was 52% democrat and 46% of the population is democrat, then you multiply the data provided by democrats by 46/52 = .8846
  • If the sample was 35% republican when 40% of the population is republican, then multiply their answers by 40/35 = 1.1429
  • If the sample was 12% independent/neither when 14% of the population is independent/neither, then multiply those responses by 14/12 = 1.1666

Then you'd get a more realistic picture. The problem with this method is that it doesn't account for people who have changed the way that they answer the "what do you describe yourself as: democrat/republican/independent/other" question. The answers to that question tend to change during an election year so weighting the results won't necessarily make them more accurate. I think polls will just present more of the raw data and leave weighting to those who want to analyze the results that way.

edit: you'll want to re-calculate all the percentages with the actual data so that rounding off to the nearest full percentage point doesn't fuck up your weighted results.

You should look at polling instead of the actual registration. The polls that ask the "what party do you identify with" question will ask the question most similar to the way it's asked in the presidential candidate poll. The actual registration tends to be very different from the way people self-identify and will vary depending on state rules (e.g. whether you have to be a registered member of a party to vote in their primary or not). The data you're looking for is the results from the presidential poll where they split-up how self-identified dems, self-identified republicans, and self-identified others answered the questions.

You want to remove all other sources for variance. It's like if you're measuring the growth rate of 2 fungi in petri dishes, you don't put one in the refrigerator and the other on the window sill you put them side by side.
